subtopics.title: The Mother Function y Equals x Squared

questions.question: For y = x², the values x = −2 and x = 2 both give y =
options: 4, because squaring wipes out the sign

questions.question: The turning point and axis of symmetry of y = x² are:
The range of y = x² is:
Which description of the curve y = x² is correct?
options: It rises steeply near zero and flattens further out
It is smooth, flattens and turns at the origin, and climbs ever more steeply on both sides
It comes to a sharp point at the origin, like a V

subtopics.title: The Effect of a — Stretch, Squash and Flip

questions.question: For y = ax², a NEGATIVE value of a means the parabola:
options: Opens upward, with a minimum turning point
Opens downward, with a maximum turning point

questions.question: Compared with y = x², the graph of y = ¼x² is:
options: Wider, because every height is quartered so the curve climbs more slowly

questions.question: For y = −3x², the value of y when x = 2 is:
When q = 0, changing a does NOT change:
options: The turning point (0; 0) or the axis of symmetry x = 0
How narrow or wide the curve is

subtopics.title: The Effect of q — Shift, Range and Intercepts

questions.question: In y = ax² + q, the parameter q:
options: Shifts the graph left or right by q units
Shifts the whole graph vertically by q units, changing nothing else
Reflects the graph in the x-axis
Changes the width of the curve

questions.question: Solving 0 = x² − 16 gives:
options: x = 4 or x = −4 — the plus-or-minus is compulsory

questions.question: Why does y = x² + 5 have NO x-intercepts?
options: Because x² = −5 has no real solution, and the upward-opening curve floats 5 units above the axis
Because its turning point is a maximum

questions.question: The turning point of y = 2x² − 8 is:
The x-intercepts of y = 2x² − 8 are:
A parabola y = ax² + q has turning point (0; −5) and passes through (2; 7). Its equation is:
Which of these is an exhibit from the error museum?
options: Reading q off the turning point
Treating q as a sideways shift — in this form the graph never moves sideways

subtopics.title: The Shape of a Thrown Ball

questions.question: The arc of a netball shot is a parabola because:
options: It climbs, turns exactly once, and falls in a mirror image of the climb
It travels in a straight line to the hoop
It speeds up all the way

questions.question: Squaring 2 and squaring −2 both give 4. On the graph this shows up as:
options: A left half that mirrors the right half across a vertical line
A straight section near the origin

subtopics.title: Turning the Bowl Over and Lifting It

questions.question: In the bowl picture, the SIGN of the number multiplying the squared part decides:
options: Whether it is a mixing bowl the right way up or a pot lid flipped over
Where the bowl crosses the vertical axis

questions.question: A number bigger than one in front of the squared part makes the bowl:
options: Tall and narrow, like a glass vase
Wide and flat, like a serving platter

questions.question: The number standing alone at the end gives you two things at once:
options: Where the curve crosses the vertical axis, and the height of the turning point

questions.question: An upright bowl LIFTED above the line has how many crossings of that line?
options: None — like a mixing bowl on the windowsill, it never reaches the floor

subtopics.title: Four Moves to a Sketch — and the Traps

questions.question: The four sketching moves, in order, are:
options: Which way up; where the turning point is; where it crosses the flat axis; one extra point plus the mirror
Crossings; direction; extra point; turning point

questions.question: For y = 2x² − 8, the extra point at x = 3 is:
Solving x² = 4 and writing only x = 2 is expensive because:
options: It throws away the second crossing, x = −2, and breaks the symmetry of the sketch

questions.question: The working gives 'x² = −5'. The correct response is:
options: State that there are no x-intercepts, because nothing real squares to a negative
